rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3.1, Table 1 - two-year (2018-2019) pot experiment in a greenhouse in Nanchang, Jiangxi, with four treatments (CK running water; LM, MM, HM micro-nano bubble concentrations) on early rice Ganxin203 and late rice WufengyouT025, reporting own grain yield, tillering, SPAD/Pn, root and nitrogen data.
rows.notes: The study reports its own data showing that micro-nano bubble (MNB) water increased pot grain yield of early rice by 4.84-10.95% and late rice by 6.10-14.31% over ordinary running water, with the HM treatment best (Table 1, Section 3.1, Abstract). The 14.31% figure in the passage is correctly taken from this study. However, the claim row's technology is drip irrigation, whereas the study applied MNB water to pots by hand every 5 days with a graduated container (Section 2.2); no drip system was used. The evidence is therefore about MNB-oxygenated water, not about drip irrigation, so Q2 is answered no and technology_mismatch is set. Had the technology been MNB/oxygenated irrigation, the profile would have been: Q3 no (single pot-yield method), Q4 yes (rhizosphere dissolved oxygen measured, Figure 1, plus root traits, SPAD/Pn as intermediate variables), Q5 no (one site, one soil, two rice crops/seasons), Q6 no (pots only), Q7 no (no stated requirement beyond concentration gradient), Q8 yes (authors state the experiment was under ideal greenhouse conditions without rain, air-source generator limited to 1000 mL/min, and field extension needs further study, Section 4.2), Q9 yes (yields reported as mean <U+00B1> SD/SE in Table 1).

notes: Full text available, though the Methods section (pages 2-3) is partly garbled by overlapping columns; key details (pot experiment, hand watering every 5 days, treatments, DO measurement) are still legible. The study never mentions drip irrigation.
